gen_risks.description: Escalating insecurity or violent conflict may block field access, delay activities and endanger staff and beneficiaries.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement security SOPs, use remote delivery tools, partner with NGOs that have safe access, and activate contingency plans for high‑risk zones.
gen_risks.evidence: Annex 3: security risk levels (green/yellow/red) and activity adaptations for insecurity.

gen_risks.description: Administrative routines and weak procurement capacity could cause procurement delays, slowing project implementation.
gen_risks.mitigation: Recruit a qualified procurement specialist, develop a detailed Procurement Manual, and provide targeted training to procurement staff.
gen_risks.evidence: Procurement Action Plan: need for qualified procurement specialist and manual of procedures to avoid delays.

gen_risks.description: Procurement in fragile areas with few bidders may lead to higher prices, reduced competition and collusion risk.
gen_risks.mitigation: Apply World Bank procurement flexibilities, pre‑qualify local suppliers, and monitor bids closely for price anomalies.
gen_risks.evidence: Procurement risk assessment notes limited bidders in fragile areas can increase prices and collusion risks.

gen_risks.description: The PIU currently lacks financial management staff and procedures, creating fiduciary risk and potential mis‑reporting.
gen_risks.mitigation: Recruit FM specialist, implement accounting software, produce a FM procedures manual, and engage an external auditor as required.
gen_risks.evidence: FA Schedule 2 Section I.A.3(c) and FM assessment highlight absence of FM staff and procedures.

gen_risks.description: Construction of warehouses and rehabilitation sites may cause water and soil pollution from solid and liquid waste.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement ESS 3 pollution‑prevention measures, conduct site‑specific environmental monitoring, and enforce waste‑management plans.
gen_risks.evidence: Section 87: key E&S risks include water and soil pollution at construction sites.

gen_risks.description: Risk of sexual exploitation, abuse or harassment (SEA/SH) among vulnerable beneficiaries could lead to harm and reputational damage.
gen_risks.mitigation: Develop and enforce an SEA/SH Action Plan, code of conduct, community sensitisation and a dedicated grievance pathway with referrals.
gen_risks.evidence: Section 87‑88: SEA/SH risk is Substantial; mitigation includes Action Plan and grievance mechanism.

gen_risks.description: Gender‑based violence (GBV) may increase among women participants, affecting their safety and project outcomes.
gen_risks.mitigation: Deploy a GBV specialist, integrate GBV screening into services, and ensure referral mechanisms to health and legal support.
gen_risks.evidence: Legal covenants require a GBV specialist; strategic context notes widespread GBV.

gen_risks.description: Interoperable digital systems (RSU, payment platforms) could be vulnerable to cyber‑attacks or data breaches.
gen_risks.mitigation: Follow ANSSI security guidelines, conduct regular security assessments, and apply data‑protection standards from CIL.
gen_risks.evidence: Sections 34‑35: security procedures by ANSSI and data‑protection authority CIL.

gen_risks.description: Increasing climate‑related shocks (droughts, floods) may raise demand for shock‑response services, straining resources.
gen_risks.mitigation: Integrate early‑warning systems, build climate‑resilient livelihoods, and maintain flexible funding buffers for emergency response.
gen_risks.evidence: Strategic Context: climate change severely undermines food security and increases shock frequency.

gen_risks.description: Fragmented coordination among ministries and partners could lead to duplication and inefficiency.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish a steering committee, schedule regular inter‑ministerial meetings, and define clear roles in the Project Implementation Manual.
gen_risks.evidence: Sections 62‑64: steering committee and inter‑ministerial coordination mechanisms.

gen_risks.description: The Unique Social Registry currently covers only ~25 % of poor households, risking exclusion of target beneficiaries.
gen_risks.mitigation: Accelerate RSU rollout, update targeting formula annually, and conduct community‑based validation to improve coverage.
gen_risks.evidence: Section 32‑33: RSU presently covers one‑quarter of poor households; goal to expand nationwide.

gen_risks.description: Beneficiaries may face barriers to opening bank or MFI accounts (KYC, ID documents), limiting financial inclusion.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide assistance for ID acquisition, simplify account opening procedures, and deliver financial literacy training.
gen_risks.evidence: Component 1 description of financial inclusion and mention of KYC challenges for women.

gen_risks.description: Insufficient private‑sector financing could limit scaling of economic inclusion activities.
gen_risks.mitigation: Engage private investors early, develop pipeline of bankable projects, and showcase pilot successes to attract capital.
gen_risks.evidence: Component 1 notes MFD‑e enabling but no private capital currently involved.

gen_risks.description: Cultural or gender norms may reduce uptake of training and savings groups, limiting impact.
gen_risks.mitigation: Conduct gender‑sensitive community outreach, involve local leaders, and adapt schedules to women’s availability (e.g., childcare).
gen_risks.evidence: Component 1.1 prioritises women and mentions adaptations such as daycare and flexible training.

gen_risks.description: Escalating insecurity could cause schedule overruns for key activities like RSU deployment and warehouse construction.
gen_risks.mitigation: Phase activities by security level, maintain a contingency buffer in the work plan, and regularly reassess timelines.
gen_risks.evidence: Annex 3 outlines activity adaptations and potential suspension under high‑intensity conflict.

gt_risks.description: Political and governance risk is assessed to be Substantial. The uncertain political and governance context provides a challenge to long-term development policy. Adaptive social protection systems are still nascent and will require continued political commitment.
gt_risks.mitigation: The team, guided by the management, will continue its high-level policy dialogue at central and decentralized levels and ensure continuous advocacy and communication.

gt_risks.description: Macroeconomic risk is assessed to be Substantial. Fiscal space remains constrained by elevated security spending and tighter financing conditions, which increase the risk of reduced budget allocations and delayed counterpart funding for new priorities and reforms, including social protection and the PAMPV. Macroeconomic risks also arise from exogenous factors, including current conflict in the Middle East which can result in a surge in oil prices and put inflationary pressure.
gt_risks.mitigation: Other programs such as the International Monetary Fund program and the World Bank's technical assistance on tax expenditure under the Sustainable Development Finance Policy can help expand fiscal space, partially mitigating these risks.

gt_risks.description: Sector strategy and policies risks are considered to be Substantial. Sectoral strategies and policies remain nascent, and the Government's budget allocation to operationalize the PAMPV remains unclear. Also, sectoral decisions are at times taken abruptly and can heavily affect implementation (for example, the suspension of cash transfers in 2023 led to an increased focus on economic inclusion, and the newly emerged priority of the CONASUR/IDPs led to the revision of the fiche de projet of this project).
gt_risks.mitigation: In parallel with high-level policy dialogue, the project supports strategic communications, adopts an agile approach, and provides technical assistance to promote evidence-based decision-making (with support from SASPP, the Social Protection Response MDTF, and the State and Peacebuilding Fund).

gt_risks.description: Overall fiduciary risks are considered as Substantial, as described in section IV.B and annex 2, based on financial assessment and procurement assessment.
gt_risks.mitigation: The project preparation fund (Grant Facility for Project Preparation) has been used not only to prepare mitigation measures to address these risks but will also elevate the project readiness (for example, effectiveness-linked actions including FM and procurement staffing and initiating the procurement packages for the first 18-months' implementation priorities) to improve the project performance.

gt_risks.description: Other risks related to insecurity are rated as High. The deteriorating and volatile security situation—particularly in regions with high poverty, displacement, and food insecurity that are project intervention areas—will likely be an important risk. The project will also address other risks related to protection of personal data: for Component 2 on social registry and interoperability, activities will be guided by the Information System Security Policy (ISSP) document developed by the ANSSI, to ensure confidentiality of households registered in the RSU.
gt_risks.mitigation: The project activities will be adjusted based on the security situation (see annex 3), and the PIU will be also staffed with a security specialist and a security management plan will be developed. To remain engaged, the project will also rely on remote delivery/monitoring, partnering with local representation (NGOs, UN agencies). The ST-RSU will conduct capacity-building activities, including training sessions and awareness campaigns, to strengthen users' ability to manage and protect households' personal data.
